main_text.p: τὸ μέρ[?], θεωρεῖν[?]standū emerit,ipse quo-que nullo pro capite suo dato ære spectatum venict. quinctiam liberos suos cū pædagogo cōdem secum postero die ducere non dubitabit.

Quæcūque autem paruo empta ferentem aliquem viderit,sibi quoq; cōmunicari iubebit. Et vbi ad ædes alienas venerit, vel ordeum, vel si vsus ita tulerit paleam mutuaturus,cos coget à quibus acceperit , id quod dederint domum sibi apportare. Sæpe etiā in balneis ad æna accedens postquam arytænā mersam repleuit, sese ipse,nō sine magno bal-ἀγὰν ἢ ἑ τοὺς εἰς τὴν ὑσεραίαν, ἡ τὸν παιδαγωγόν. ἡ ὅστις ἐωνημένῳ· ἀξιά τις φέρει, μεταδοῦναι πελεῦσαι ἔ αὐτ᾽. ἔ ὅτι ἡ ἀλλοτρίαν οἰκίαν ἐλθὼν, δανείσας κείθας, ᾧ τοῖ ἀχρεῖον ἐ ταῦτα χρήσας, ἀναγκάσαι ἀποφέρειν πρὸς αὐτόν. ἁμνὸς ἢ ἐ πρὸς τὰ χαλκία ἃ ἐν τῷ βαλανέῳ προσελθὼν, καὶ βάψας ἀρύταιναν, βοῶντ᾽ τῷ βαλανέως, {*}αὐτὸς * αὐτῇ καταχέασαι, ἐ εἰπεῖν, ὅτι λέλουταί ἀπὼν· χάρει, ἡδέα σοι χαρεῖς.χ.αὐτὸν
neatoris clamore, perfundit: dein discedens, Laui, inquit: & ad balneatorem conversus, Ego verò, ait, gratiam tibi nullam.

page.notes: Ligatures ct and st are read as c+t and s+t. The Greek marginal note is uncertain in several letters, marked [?]. The words "venict" and "postero" are read from the ligatures and may be printing variants. "arytænā" is read as printed. The Greek column's first line and the Latin fragment "neatoris" begin mid-line. Greek readings marked [?] are uncertain where the print is faint; the Greek word after "βοῶντ᾽" and the Latin translation below may not correspond word for word. The asterisk in the text appears twice; only one reference mark is transcribed. Greek accents and breathings are copied as seen but may be imperfect.
